claim: Try the sample project and find Save at bottom right.
sandbox: Fresh browser context opens /demo/, searches the bundled sample for Save, and asserts the directional result and walkthrough.

claim: The website sample demo sends no data to third parties.
sandbox: Fresh browser records every request while using /demo/ and accepts only the product origin.

claim: The website demo does not save searches or sample changes.
sandbox: Fresh context changes the search, reloads, and confirms the default is restored with no user-data keys or cookies.

claim: The website has no advertising cookies, behavioral analytics, or third-party scripts.
sandbox: Fresh browser confirms an empty cookie jar, only same-origin script sources, and no analytics or tracker scripts.

claim: The website sample demo reloads offline after its first visit.
sandbox: A dedicated browser context visits /demo/, waits for the worker, goes offline, reloads, and finds the demo heading.

claim: Online visitors receive the current site shell after an update.
sandbox: Browser regression reads the shipped worker and asserts a versioned cache with network-first document requests.

claim: The desktop app includes a sample project that finds Save without a capture.
sandbox: Fresh desktop interface opens ?demo=1, searches bundled sample labels, and asserts the Save result.

claim: Desktop demo data stays separate and is discarded when Start for real is chosen.
where: Desktop demo banner, README, and demo documentation
sandbox: Fresh app context sets a real preference, changes the demo preference, exits, and confirms demo storage is cleared.

claim: Voice-speed control is free.
where: Desktop preferences and landing download section
sandbox: Fresh desktop interface changes the enabled voice-speed slider without a license or account.

claim: The desktop sample supports shortcuts to read labels, find text, and describe likely buttons.
where: Landing shortcut map and desktop buttons
sandbox: Fresh sample sends all three documented Alt+Shift shortcuts and asserts their result or focus state.

claim: Screen-reader announcements accompany results.
sandbox: A recorded speech adapter and the polite live region both receive the Save direction.

claim: Empty Find requests explain what to do next.
sandbox: Bundled sample submits an empty Find and asserts the exact recovery instruction.

claim: OCR output is labeled as uncertain text, without a fabricated confidence percentage.
where: Desktop result list and landing FAQ
sandbox: Fresh sample asserts the OCR warning and rejects the old quality-estimate wording.

claim: Bundled recognition models process a fixture locally without a service.
where: Landing privacy statements, privacy policy, and README
sandbox: Vitest executes the native Rust test that loads both bundled models and analyzes an in-memory fixture.

claim: Capture uses the one visible window the person selects.
where: Landing steps, desktop chooser, privacy policy, and README
sandbox: Native controlled-window test selects the requested id among two windows and rejects an absent id.

claim: Captured pixels are absent from the result returned after recognition.
where: Landing privacy section, privacy policy, and README
sandbox: Native result-boundary test serializes a fixture analysis and confirms labels are present while capture, pixels, and image bytes are absent.

claim: Lens gives directions without controlling another app.
sandbox: Fresh sample finds Cancel, changes only guidance state, keeps its URL, and makes no external request.

claim: All shipped label-finding features work without an account or purchase.
where: Landing, privacy policy, terms, and README
sandbox: Fresh sample with no account state exercises read, likely-button, find, and voice-speed tools.

claim: The landing page checks GitHub release metadata at most once per hour per browser.
sandbox: Browser intercepts the GitHub API, reloads, and asserts one request plus a one-hour local cache.

claim: When release metadata is unavailable, the landing page keeps a direct Release page link.
sandbox: Browser removes bootstrap metadata, returns an empty API result, and asserts the fallback link and zero console errors.

claim: Unknown website addresses receive the designed 404 response.
sandbox: Browser requests an unknown document and asserts HTTP 404, route metadata, shared navigation, and shared footer.

claim: Release 0.1.8 provides macOS, Windows, and Linux packages tied to this source commit.
sandbox: GitHub release API, published latest.json, SHA256SUMS, and the live release identity are compared with the clean checkout commit and required package names.

claim: Version 0.1.8 packages have no publisher signature.
sandbox: The claim reads CI-produced Linux, macOS, and Windows signature reports attached to the published release.

claim: The supplied installers verify SHA-256 before installation.
sandbox: Shell installer runs locally against valid and tampered fixtures; the release supplies the equivalent Windows CI outcome report.

claim: Recognition dependency licenses are recorded in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.
sandbox: Cargo metadata for locked ocrs and rten versions and licenses is compared with the notice table.

claim: The shipped hero has a retained generation and review record.
where: Footer, README, design record, and assets/src
sandbox: The source image hash, model record, and no-text prompt are matched to the shipped provenance files.
